chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin al-Thaqafi, from Abu Basir, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:
Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) said: I am the martyr of the tear. No believer mentions me except that he sheds tears.

key_terms.استعبر: To shed tears, to weep, from the root ayn-ba-ra relating to tears and crying
key_terms.قتيل العبرة: The martyr of the tear, a title for Imam Husayn (AS) indicating the perpetual grief evoked by his martyrdom

ai.seo_question: Why is Imam Husayn called the martyr of the tear (qatil al-abra)?
ai.summary: Imam Husayn (AS) describes himself as 'the martyr of the tear' (qatil al-abra), meaning his martyrdom at Karbala is of such profound tragedy that no true believer can recall it without weeping. This statement, narrated through a chain going back through Imam al-Sadiq and the previous Imams, highlights the spiritual significance of mourning Imam Husayn in Shia tradition. The assembly was held on the 5th of Muharram, 368 AH, directly connected to the annual Muharram commemorations.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abu’l Khattab from al-Hakam b. Miskin al-Thaqafi from Abu Basir from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his fathers (as).  He said:
Abu `Abdillah al-Husayn b. `Ali (as) said: I am the martyr of the tear. No believer shall mention me but that he shall shed tears.
